title: Bernard Shaw and Isadora Duncan: Brains and Beauty!
summary: When the glamorous dancer proposed they have a child combining 'my beauty and your brains', Shaw replied: 'What if it inherited my beauty and your brains?'
keywords: Bernard Shaw and Isadora Duncan: Brains and Beauty!
full_text:
George Bernard Shaw was universally celebrated as the greatest dramatist of the English-speaking world; yet physically, he was lean, pale, and possessed an eccentric, wild-bearded countenance.

During the 1920s, the American dancer Isadora Duncan was celebrated as the ultimate embodiment of classical feminine beauty, captivating theaters across Paris, London, and New York.

Intrigued by Shaw's intellect, Duncan sent the playwright an audacious and flirtatious proposal:

"My dear Mr. Shaw!
We two ought to have a child together!
Just imagine: with my extraordinary beauty and your towering intellect, what a magnificent wonder of the world our child would be!"

Shaw read the letter with amused delight. Picking up his fountain pen, he drafted an instantaneous response:

"My dear Madam!
Your proposal is undeniably flattering.
Yet I shudder when I contemplate the terrifying genetic catastrophe that might ensue!
What if, by some cruel trick of nature, that unfortunate child should inherit...
**My beauty, and your brains?**
Pray forgive me, madam; the risk is far too immense to contemplate!"

Duncan burst into laughter upon reading the reply. Shaw's instantaneous reversal demonstrated how intellectual agility can puncture vanity with effortless grace.
moral: Vanity is easily dismantled when confronted by humble realism and brilliant comedic irony.
